Headline: Widespread Drought Occurring Throughout the U.S.

I notice that the areas with extreme and exceptional drought are scattered around the country. There is not a specific area with much more drought than others. However, the middle is more concentrated in severe droughts, but not by much. I wonder why this is, considering each area of the country has a different climate. I would expect the southwest region to experience more exceptional or extreme droughts. I also wonder why one of Texas's tips, touching the ocean, has no drought. Despite being slightly left, the other tip has exceptional drought. This graph is trying to show us that drought is no longer limited to one area of the country. However, drought affects nearly every part of the country. This is relevant to me and my community, as I reside in New Jersey. There is a severe drought in New Jersey, specifically in the lower half. In the past two months, weeks have gone without rain. This could be the reason for the occurrence of a severe drought in New Jersey, as historically, droughts have not been frequent in the state.
